new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: (75 pp., text layer; extracted). Both quoted passages are present at the stated locators. p.58 §1.2(vii) ( lines 177-182): "Korom is probably a dialect of Ɓa spoken in about four villages in the easternmost part of the Ɓa area. It is also spoken in Tilé Nougar by the Kawãwãy [kàwa̰ː́ wày] (pl.), a small group living among the Fanya and belonging to the blacksmith caste (Lionnet, field notes). Since we only know Korom as it is spoken by the Kawãwãy, we will tentatively use the term Kawãwãy to refer to the Korom data presented in this paper." -- verbatim except the text layer has a space inside the phonetic form [kàwa̰ː́ wày] (extraction artefact). p.71 §4.4 Tones (lines 684-688):…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kawaway (= Korom as spoken by the Kawãwãy blacksmiths) is treated as a variety of Ɓa, a language with three contrastive level tones plus contours; the Kawãwãy data in the paper are transcribed with H/M/L tones. No source says anything about word stress or accent placement in Kawaway or in Ɓa; the only prominence-related remark (Lionnet 2025 ms. p.13) is that Ɓa has areal 'stem-initial prominence' in the phonotactic sense (full segment inventory only in the stem-initial syllable), which is not a word-stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the tone statement is made for Ɓa/Lua/Tun/Bolgo generally, and Kawaway's membership in Ɓa is itself hedged ('probably a dialect of Ɓa').
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/grammatical tone at word level; no stress domain discussed. Statement applies to Ɓa as a whole, extended to Kawaway only via the authors' 'Ɓa (including Kawãwãy)'.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog kawa1291 'Kawaway' = Kawa̰wa̰y/Kawãwãy [kàwa̰ː́wày], the name of a ~60-person blacksmith-caste group living among the Fanya at Tilé Nougar (also Bar, Sarabara, Sakré Deleb); the language they speak is Korom, which Boyeldieu et al. 2018 (p.58) and Boyeldieu et al. 2020 (p.184) regard as probably a dialect/variety of Ɓa (Bua proper, glottocode buaa1246 area; Glottolog groups kawa1291 with Ɓa under 'Ba-Korom' buai1235). The tone statement quoted is made for Ɓa (with Lua, Tun, Bolgo), not for Kawaway by name.
